literature.headline_zh: 人偏肺病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期人偏肺病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 总体而言,218/1683(13.0%)的住院ARI儿童和81/1165(7.0%)的门诊ARI儿童检测出HMPV阳性。HMPV通常在12月至5月间流行;季节性和发病率在2019冠状病毒病(COVID-19)大流行期间受到干扰。在泊松模型中,年龄小于2岁(调整风险比:1.43 [1.08-1.90])和发病后4天以上才就诊(1.38 [1.09-1.75])与HMPV相关住院的风险显著增加,相较于HMPV相关的门诊访问。 [10.1097/inf.0000000000005469]

我们发现,将气候变量纳入HMPV动态模型的模型,包括水汽压、降水量、潜在蒸散发量和最低温度,无法解释所有地区HMPV活动的时间。相反,HMPV活动的时间与RSV活动相关,RSV的存在会降低HMPV的动态率。我们证明,在考虑的候选模型中,只有包含RSV相关项的模型能够再现某些地区观察到的HMPV的两年周期模式,这种模式表现为交替的“晚期小规模”和“早期大规模”疫情。 [10.1371/journal.ppat.1014810]

在预测试中,59%的参与者知识得分处于平均水平,36%得分良好,4%得分较差,1%得分非常好。预测试的知识平均得分是11.65 ± 2.931,范围从04到21。在后测试中,57%的得分良好,27%的得分非常好,16%的得分处于平均水平,0%的得分较差或优秀。后测试的平均得分是16.36 ± 3.267,范围从09到22。研究发现,后测试的知识得分与大多数人口统计学变量无显著关联,除了父母的教育水平。 [10.21275/sr261031085904]
结果显示,SeV及其重组体疫苗在动物模型中诱导了快速且持久的免疫应答,并在儿童中表现出良好的耐受性和免疫原性。 [10.3389/fmicb.2026.2002178]

该检测方法对所有三个目标的检测限为100 copies/mL,以核酸提取前原始样本的等效浓度表示。在评估条件下,未观察到对14种指定非目标病原体的交叉反应,并检测到了所有8种目标菌株。重复性测试显示,在低和中等浓度下,Ct值的变异系数(CV)≤2%。在单个目标水平上,所开发检测方法的敏感性分别为HRV 98.82%、PIV 98.55%和MPV 100.0%,特异性均为100.0%。 [10.1016/j.jviromet.2026.115504]

brief_items_zh: 本期人偏肺病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。

总体而言,218/1683(13.0%)的住院ARI儿童和81/1165(7.0%)的门诊ARI儿童检测出HMPV阳性。HMPV通常在12月至5月间流行;季节性和发病率在2019冠状病毒病(COVID-19)大流行期间受到干扰。在泊松模型中,年龄小于2岁(调整风险比:1.43 [1.08-1.90])和发病后4天以上才就诊(1.38 [1.09-1.75])与HMPV相关住院的风险显著增加,相较于HMPV相关的门诊访问。
我们发现,将气候变量纳入HMPV动态模型的模型,包括水汽压、降水量、潜在蒸散发量和最低温度,无法解释所有地区HMPV活动的时间。相反,HMPV活动的时间与RSV活动相关,RSV的存在会降低HMPV的动态率。我们证明,在考虑的候选模型中,只有包含RSV相关项的模型能够再现某些地区观察到的HMPV的两年周期模式,这种模式表现为交替的“晚期小规模”和“早期大规模”疫情。

在预测试中,59%的参与者知识得分处于平均水平,36%得分良好,4%得分较差,1%得分非常好。预测试的知识平均得分是11.65 ± 2.931,范围从04到21。在后测试中,57%的得分良好,27%的得分非常好,16%的得分处于平均水平,0%的得分较差或优秀。后测试的平均得分是16.36 ± 3.267,范围从09到22。研究发现,后测试的知识得分与大多数人口统计学变量无显著关联,除了父母的教育水平。
结果显示,SeV及其重组体疫苗在动物模型中诱导了快速且持久的免疫应答,并在儿童中表现出良好的耐受性和免疫原性。 [10.3389/fmicb.2026.2002178]。

papers.title: Human Metapneumovirus–associated Infections Among American Indian and Alaska Native Children, 2019–2024
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Data on human metapneumovirus (HMPV)-associated acute respiratory infections (ARI) among American Indian/Alaska Native (AI/AN) children are lacking publications. METHODS: We conducted active ARI surveillance among hospitalized and outpatient AI/AN children <5 years of age at select facilities in Navajo Nation, White Mountain Apache Tribal lands, and Alaska (Anchorage and Yukon-Kuskokwim Delta). Children meeting a symptom-based ARI case definition from November 2019 to May 2024 were eligible. Data were collected via questionnaire and chart review. Mid-turbinate nasal swabs were tested for HMPV and other respiratory pathogens by polymerase chain reaction. Incidence rates of HMPV-associated hospitalization were calculated using Poisson regression. Seasonality was described, and risk factors for HMPV-associated hospitalization were assessed using Poisson multivariable modeling with robust standard errors. RESULTS: Overall, 13.0% (218/1683) of children hospitalized with ARI and 7.0% (81/1165) of outpatient children with ARI were HMPV-positive. HMPV generally circulated December through May; seasonality and incidence were disrupted by the coronavirus disease 2019 pandemic. In 2023-2024, incidence rates of HMPV-associated ARI hospitalization per 1000 children <5 years old were 11.3 (95% confidence interval: 8.6-14.8) in the Southwest, 10.3 (7.4-14.4) in the Yukon-Kuskokwim Delta, and 0 (0-1.1) in Anchorage. In the Poisson model, age <2 years (adjusted risk ratio: 1.43 [1.08-1.90]) and presenting to care ≥4 days after illness onset (1.38 [1.09-1.75]) were significantly associated with increased risk for HMPV-associated hospitalization compared with HMPV-associated outpatient visits. CONCLUSIONS: This analysis documents the burden of HMPV-associated ARI and hospitalization among AI/AN children <5 years of age as a baseline to inform the use of future pediatric HMPV prevention products.

papers.abstract_original: BACKGROUND: Data on human metapneumovirus (HMPV)-associated acute respiratory infections (ARI) among American Indian/Alaska Native (AI/AN) children are lacking publications. METHODS: We conducted active ARI surveillance among hospitalized and outpatient AI/AN children <5 years of age at select facilities in Navajo Nation, White Mountain Apache Tribal lands, and Alaska (Anchorage and Yukon-Kuskokwim Delta). Children meeting a symptom-based ARI case definition from November 2019 to May 2024 were eligible. Data were collected via questionnaire and chart review. Mid-turbinate nasal swabs were tested for HMPV and other respiratory pathogens by polymerase chain reaction. Incidence rates of HMPV-associated hospitalization were calculated using Poisson regression. Seasonality was described, and risk factors for HMPV-associated hospitalization were assessed using Poisson multivariable modeling with robust standard errors. RESULTS: Overall, 13.0% (218/1683) of children hospitalized with ARI and 7.0% (81/1165) of outpatient children with ARI were HMPV-positive. HMPV generally circulated December through May; seasonality and incidence were disrupted by the coronavirus disease 2019 pandemic. In 2023-2024, incidence rates of HMPV-associated ARI hospitalization per 1000 children <5 years old were 11.3 (95% confidence interval: 8.6-14.8) in the Southwest, 10.3 (7.4-14.4) in the Yukon-Kuskokwim Delta, and 0 (0-1.1) in Anchorage. In the Poisson model, age <2 years (adjusted risk ratio: 1.43 [1.08-1.90]) and presenting to care ≥4 days after illness onset (1.38 [1.09-1.75]) were significantly associated with increased risk for HMPV-associated hospitalization compared with HMPV-associated outpatient visits. CONCLUSIONS: This analysis documents the burden of HMPV-associated ARI and hospitalization among AI/AN children <5 years of age as a baseline to inform the use of future pediatric HMPV prevention products.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to address the lack of data on human metapneumovirus (HMPV)-associated acute respiratory infections (ARI) among American Indian/Alaska Native (AI/AN) children. Active ARI surveillance was conducted among hospitalized and outpatient AI/AN children under 5 years of age in Navajo Nation, White Mountain Apache Tribal lands, and Alaska from November 2019 to May 2024. Data were collected via questionnaires and chart reviews, with nasal swabs tested for HMPV and other respiratory pathogens using polymerase chain reaction. Incidence rates were calculated using Poisson regression, and seasonality and risk factors were assessed with multivariable modeling. Results showed that 13.0% of hospitalized children and 7.0% of outpatient children were HMPV-positive, with seasonality disrupted by the coronavirus disease 2019 pandemic. Age <2 years and delayed care were significantly associated with increased risk of HMPV-associated hospitalization. The authors concluded that these findings serve as a baseline for future pediatric HMPV prevention strategies. The study's limitations include its focus on specific locations, which may limit generalizability, and its observational design, which may introduce confounding factors. The evidence is moderate in strength.

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:关于美国原住民/阿拉斯加原住民(AI/AN)儿童中与人偏肺病毒(HMPV)相关的急性呼吸道感染(ARI)的数据缺乏相关文献。方法:我们在纳瓦霍族地区、怀特山阿帕奇部落地区和阿拉斯加(安克雷奇和尤通凯斯克威姆河三角洲)的选定医疗机构中,对住院和门诊的<5岁AI/AN儿童进行了主动的ARI监测。从2019年11月至2024年5月,符合基于症状的ARI病例定义的儿童有资格参与研究。数据通过问卷和病历回顾收集。对中鼻甲鼻拭子进行聚合酶链反应检测HMPV和其他呼吸道病原体。使用泊松回归计算与HMPV相关的住院率。描述了季节性特征,并通过泊松多变量模型(稳健标准误差)评估了与HMPV相关住院的风险因素。结果:总体而言,13.0%(218/1683)的住院ARI儿童和7.0%(81/1165)的门诊ARI儿童检测出HMPV阳性。HMPV通常在12月至5月间流行;季节性和与HMPV相关的住院率在2019冠状病毒病大流行期间受到干扰。在2023-2024年,<5岁儿童中与HMPV相关的ARI住院率每1000人分别为西南地区11.3(95%置信区间:8.6-14.8)、尤通凯斯克威姆河三角洲10.3(7.4-14.4)和安克雷奇0(0-1.1)。在泊松模型中,年龄<2岁(调整风险比:1.43 [1.08-1.90])和发病后≥4天才就诊(1.38 [1.09-1.75])与HMPV相关的住院风险显著增加,与HMPV相关的门诊访问相比。结论:本分析记录了AI/AN<5岁儿童中与HMPV相关的ARI和住院负担,为未来儿童HMPV预防产品的使用提供了基础信息。

papers.title: Spatiotemporal dynamics of human metapneumovirus and potential impact of respiratory syncytial virus interventions in the United States
papers.abstract: Human metapneumovirus (HMPV) causes acute lower respiratory infections, primarily affecting young children and older adults, with seasonal outbreaks peaking annually in March or April in the United States and other temperate regions in the Northern hemisphere. However, the factors driving HMPV seasonality in the United States remain poorly understood. We analyzed laboratory-confirmed HMPV cases and age-specific emergency department visits across 10 US regions, fitting an age-stratified dynamic transmission model to assess spatiotemporal patterns and investigate the influence of environmental variables and viral interference from RSV on HMPV transmission rates. We found that models incorporating climate variables into the transmission rate, including vapor pressure, precipitation, potential evapotranspiration, and minimum temperature, could not capture the timing of HMPV activity across all regions. Instead, HMPV timing was associated with RSV activity, with the HMPV transmission rate reduced in the presence of RSV. We showed that among the candidate models considered, only the models that included an RSV-associated term could reproduce the biennial pattern of HMPV observed in some regions, characterized by alternating “late-small” and “early-large” epidemics. When the best-fit model including the RSV-associated term was used to predict the potential impact of RSV interventions on HMPV transmission, we found that RSV interventions are unlikely to result in a substantial increase in HMPV activity despite reducing competition from RSV. Our work unravels the spatiotemporal dynamics of HMPV and its interaction with RSV, informing future seasonal forecasting and intervention strategies for HMPV.

papers.title: A one-step multiplex real-time reverse transcription quantitative PCR assay for rapid and simultaneous detection of human parainfluenza virus, human metapneumovirus, and rhinovirus in patients with acute respiratory tract infection
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Clinically, acute respiratory tract infections (ARIs) caused by human parainfluenza virus (PIV), human metapneumovirus (MPV), and human rhinoviruses (HRV) are often indistinguishable due to overlapping symptoms. This study aimed to develop a one-step multiplex real-time RT-qPCR assay for simultaneous, rapid, and accurate detection of PIV (types 1-4), MPV (subgroups A and B), and HRV (species A and B). METHODS: A one-step multiplex real-time RT-qPCR assay was established for simultaneous detection of PIV, MPV, and HRV in clinical specimens. Primers and probes targeted conserved genomic regions, and an internal reference gene (B2M) was included for quality assurance. The limit of detection was determined via serial dilution of standard strains. Assay specificity was verified using 14 non-target pathogens, and repeatability was evaluated across various specimen concentrations. Clinical validation involved comparison with a commercial kit, with sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, agreement rate, and Kappa coefficient calculated for assessment. RESULTS: A one-step multiplex real-time RT-qPCR assay was successfully developed for the simultaneous detection of PIV, MPV, and HRV. The assay demonstrated a detection limit of 100 copies/mL for all three targets, expressed as the equivalent concentration in the original specimen before nucleic acid extraction; this LOD was determined under multiplex co-amplification conditions, with all three targets present in the same reaction tube at every concentration level. No cross-reactivity was observed against the 14 specified non-target pathogens under the conditions evaluated, and all eight target strains were detected. Repeatability testing showed coefficients of variation (CV) of ≤ 2% for Ct values at low and medium concentrations. At the individual-target level, the sensitivity of the developed assay was 98.82% for HRV, 98.55% for PIV, and 100.0% for MPV, with specificity of 100.0% for all three targets. Pooled (target-level) sensitivity and specificity were 99.06% and 100.0%, respectively, and the overall agreement with the reference method was 99.24% (260/262). CONCLUSION: The method provides a technical approach for the simultaneous detection of PIV, MPV, and HRV species A and B. Its clinical utility relative to comprehensive respiratory pathogen panels remains to be established.

papers.abstract_zh: 目的:临床中,由人副流感病毒(PIV)、人偏肺病毒(MPV)和人鼻病毒(HRV)引起的急性呼吸道感染(ARIs)由于症状重叠而常常难以区分。本研究旨在开发一种一步法多重实时RT-qPCR检测方法,用于同时、快速且准确地检测PIV(1-4型)、MPV(A和B亚组)以及HRV(A和B种)。方法:建立了一种一步法多重实时RT-qPCR检测方法,用于临床样本中PIV、MPV和HRV的同时检测。引物和探针针对保守的基因组区域,且包含一个内部参考基因(B2M)以确保检测质量。通过标准菌株的连续稀释确定检测限。使用14种非目标病原体验证检测特异性,并在不同样本浓度下评估重复性。临床验证通过与商业试剂盒进行比较,计算敏感性、特异性、预测值、符合率和Kappa系数以进行评估。结果:成功开发了一种用于同时检测PIV、MPV和HRV的一步法多重实时RT-qPCR检测方法。该检测方法对所有三个目标的检测限为100 copies/mL,以核酸提取前原始样本的等效浓度表示;该检测限是在多重共扩增条件下确定的,所有三个目标在每个浓度水平下均存在于同一反应管中。在评估条件下,未观察到对14种指定非目标病原体的交叉反应,并检测到了所有8种目标菌株。重复性测试显示,在低和中等浓度下,Ct值的变异系数(CV)≤2%。在单个目标水平上,所开发检测方法的敏感性分别为HRV 98.82%、PIV 98.55%和MPV 100.0%,特异性均为100.0%。合并(目标水平)的敏感性和特异性分别为99.06%和100.0%,与参考方法的总体符合率为99.24%(260/262)。结论:该方法为同时检测PIV、MPV和HRV A、B种提供了一种技术途径。其相对于全面呼吸道病原体检测面板的临床实用性仍有待确立。

analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 建立了一种一步法多重实时RT-qPCR检测方法,用于临床样本中PIV、MPV和HRV的同时检测。本研究旨在开发一种用于快速准确检测这些病毒的检测方法,用于急性呼吸道感染患者的诊断。
analysis_zh.methods: 引物和探针针对保守的基因组区域,且包含一个内部参考基因(B2M)以确保检测质量。通过标准菌株的连续稀释确定检测限。使用14种非目标病原体验证检测特异性,并在不同样本浓度下评估重复性。临床验证通过与商业试剂盒进行比较,计算敏感性、特异性、预测值、符合率和Kappa系数以进行评估。

papers.title: A Study to Assess the Effectiveness of Planned Teaching Programme on Knowledge regarding Human Metapneumovirus among Parents of School Going Children Age Group of 6-12 Years in Selected Community Area: A Pre-Experimental
papers.abstract: Human metapneumovirus is a negative-sense single-stranded RNA virus of the family Pneumoviridae and is closely related to the avian metapneumovirus subgroup C. Globally In 2018, there were an estimated 14.2 million acute lower respiratory infection cases associated with human metapneumovirus in children under 5 years old. In one study, 113 out of 4519 samples tested were positive for human metapneumovirus. Human metapneumovirus is a major global cause of respiratory infections with an overall pooled prevalence of about 5.3% among patients with respiratory illness and a higher prevalence of 5-25% in children. Objectives: To assess the knowledge of parents of school going children's age group of 6-12 years regarding Human Metapneumovirus selected community area, to assess the effectiveness of Planned Teaching Programme on knowledge regarding Human Metapneumovirus among parents of school going children age group of 6-12 years in selected community area, to determine the association between knowledge levels and selected demographic variables regarding Human Metapneumovirus among parents of school going children age group of 6-12 years in selected community area. Materials and Methods: A pre-experimental one-group pretest and post-test resign design were used. 100 parents of school going children participated in this study. The sample size was calculated by using Cochran's sample size formula. Quantitative research design was used. Non-Probability convenient sampling technique was used to select the sample. The data were collected from selected community area, using socio demographic data sheet and structured knowledge questionnaires. Consent was obtained from participant in the study. Results: In this study, majority of the subjects 28% were from the age group of 10-11 years and 12 years, majority of the subjects 55% were female, majority of the subjects 66% were belongs to Hindu religion, majority of the subjects 40% were study up to secondary education, majority of the subjects 28% were work as a housewife and majority of the subjects 55% having no any knowledge about human metapneumovirus. In pre-test, majority 59% of subjects had average level of knowledge score, 36% had good level of knowledge score, 4% had poor level of knowledge score, 1% had very good level of knowledge score and 0% had excellent level of knowledge score. analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to evaluate the knowledge of parents of school-going children aged 6-12 years regarding human metapneumovirus and to determine the effectiveness of a planned teaching programme in improving this knowledge. Human metapneumovirus is a significant cause of respiratory infections, particularly in children, and understanding parental knowledge is crucial for public health interventions.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A pre-experimental one-group pretest and post-test design was employed in a selected community area. The study involved 100 parents of school-going children aged 6-12 years, with a focus on assessing their knowledge levels before and after the intervention.
analysis.methods: The study used a quantitative research design with non-probability convenient sampling. Data were collected using socio-demographic data sheets and structured knowledge questionnaires. Consent was obtained from all participants, and the study was conducted in a selected community area.
analysis.main_results: In the pre-test, 59% of participants had average knowledge scores, 36% had good scores, 4% had poor scores, and 1% had very good scores. The mean pre-test knowledge score was 11.65 ± 2.931, ranging from 04 to 21. In the post-test, 57% had good scores, 27% had very good scores, 16% had average scores, and 0% had poor or excellent scores. The mean post-test score was 16.36 ± 3.267, ranging from 09 to 22. The study found no significant association between post-test knowledge scores and most demographic variables, except for the education level of the parents.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The planned teaching programme was interpreted as effective in improving parental knowledge about human metapneumovirus. The novelty of the study lies in its focus on assessing the impact of a structured educational intervention on parental awareness of this virus.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that targeted educational interventions can enhance parental knowledge about human metapneumovirus, which is important for promoting awareness and potentially improving prevention and management strategies in the community.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study used a non-probability sampling method, which may limit the generalizability of the results. Additionally, the lack of a control group and the reliance on self-reported knowledge scores may introduce bias. The evidence is moderate in strength due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to assess the knowledge of parents of school-going children aged 6-12 years regarding human metapneumovirus and evaluate the effectiveness of a planned teaching programme in improving this knowledge. A pre-experimental one-group pretest and post-test design was used, involving 100 parents in a selected community area. Data were collected using socio-demographic data sheets and structured knowledge questionnaires. The pre-test results showed that 59% of participants had average knowledge scores, while the post-test results indicated an improvement, with 57% having good scores and 27% having very good scores. The study found no significant association between post-test knowledge scores and most demographic variables, except for the education level of the parents. The planned teaching programme was interpreted as effective in enhancing parental knowledge about human metapneumovirus. The findings suggest that targeted educational interventions can improve awareness of this virus, which is important for public health strategies. However, the study's non-probability sampling and lack of a control group limit the generalizability and strength of the evidence, resulting in a moderate confidence assessment.

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to evaluate the knowledge of parents of school-going children aged 6-12 years regarding human metapneumovirus and to determine the effectiveness of a planned teaching programme in improving this knowledge. Human metapneumovirus is a significant cause of respiratory infections, particularly in children, and understanding parental knowledge is crucial for public health interventions.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: A pre-experimental one-group pretest and post-test design was employed in a selected community area. The study involved 100 parents of school-going children aged 6-12 years, with a focus on assessing their knowledge levels before and after the intervention.
analysis_en.methods: The study used a quantitative research design with non-probability convenient sampling. Data were collected using socio-demographic data sheets and structured knowledge questionnaires. Consent was obtained from all participants, and the study was conducted in a selected community area.
analysis_en.main_results: In the pre-test, 59% of participants had average knowledge scores, 36% had good scores, 4% had poor scores, and 1% had very good scores. The mean pre-test knowledge score was 11.65 ± 2.931, ranging from 04 to 21. In the post-test, 57% had good scores, 27% had very good scores, 16% had average scores, and 0% had poor or excellent scores. The mean post-test score was 16.36 ± 3.267, ranging from 09 to 22. The study found no significant association between post-test knowledge scores and most demographic variables, except for the education level of the parents.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The planned teaching programme was interpreted as effective in improving parental knowledge about human metapneumovirus. The novelty of the study lies in its focus on assessing the impact of a structured educational intervention on parental awareness of this virus.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that targeted educational interventions can enhance parental knowledge about human metapneumovirus, which is important for promoting awareness and potentially improving prevention and management strategies in the community.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study used a non-probability sampling method, which may limit the generalizability of the results. Additionally, the lack of a control group and the reliance on self-reported knowledge scores may introduce bias. The evidence is moderate in strength due to these limitations.

papers.title_zh: 评估计划教学方案对6-12岁学龄儿童家长关于人偏肺病毒知识效果的研究:一项预实验设计
papers.source_body_en: Human metapneumovirus is a negative-sense single-stranded RNA virus of the family Pneumoviridae and is closely related to the avian metapneumovirus subgroup C. Globally In 2018, there were an estimated 14.2 million acute lower respiratory infection cases associated with human metapneumovirus in children under 5 years old. In one study, 113 out of 4519 samples tested were positive for human metapneumovirus. Human metapneumovirus is a major global cause of respiratory infections with an overall pooled prevalence of about 5.3% among patients with respiratory illness and a higher prevalence of 5-25% in children. Objectives: To assess the knowledge of parents of school going children's age group of 6-12 years regarding Human Metapneumovirus selected community area, to assess the effectiveness of Planned Teaching Programme on knowledge regarding Human Metapneumovirus among parents of school going children age group of 6-12 years in selected community area, to determine the association between knowledge levels and selected demographic variables regarding Human Metapneumovirus among parents of school going children age group of 6-12 years in selected community area. Materials and Methods: A pre-experimental one-group pretest and post-test resign design were used. 100 parents of school going children participated in this study. The sample size was calculated by using Cochran's sample size formula. Quantitative research design was used. Non-Probability convenient sampling technique was used to select the sample. The data were collected from selected community area, using socio demographic data sheet and structured knowledge questionnaires. Consent was obtained from participant in the study. Results: In this study, majority of the subjects 28% were from the age group of 10-11 years and 12 years, majority of the subjects 55% were female, majority of the subjects 66% were belongs to Hindu religion, majority of the subjects 40% were study up to secondary education, majority of the subjects 28% were work as a housewife and majority of the subjects 55% having no any knowledge about human metapneumovirus. In pre-test, majority 59% of subjects had average level of knowledge score, 36% had good level of knowledge score, 4% had poor level of knowledge score, 1% had very good level of knowledge score and 0% had excellent level of knowledge score. Mean knowledge score in pre-test of the subjects was 11.65 + 2.931. Minimum knowledge score in pre-test was 04 and maximum knowledge score in pre-test was 21. While in post-test, majority 57% of subjects had good level of knowledge score, 27% had very good level of knowledge score, 16% had average level of knowledge score and 0% had poor and excellent level of knowledge score. Mean knowledge score in post-test of the subjects was 16.36 + 3.267. Minimum knowledge score in post-test was 09 and maximum knowledge score in post-test was 22. Conclusion: The written prepared material by the investigator in the form of planned teaching helped the subject to improve their knowledge regarding Human Metapneumovirus among parents of school-going children. The study also found no significant association between post-test knowledge scores and most demographic variables, except for the education of parents, which showed a significant influence. The planned teaching programme proved to be an effective method for enhancing parental knowledge on Human Metapneumovirus.

papers.title: Sendai virus, a candidate vaccine for the prevention of respiratory virus infections in children: a review
papers.abstract: Background Respiratory viruses including human parainfluenza virus (hPIV), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and human metapneumovirus (hMPV), pose serious, potentially lethal threats to humans, particularly infants and young children. While maternal vaccines and monoclonal antibodies are advancing to provide transient protection against these viruses, licensed pediatric vaccines are not yet available. Sendai virus (SeV) is now being developed as an intranasal (I.N.) vaccine candidate for the prevention of serious respiratory viral infections in children. Methods To examine the potential of replication-competent Sendai virus and its recombinants as pediatric respiratory virus vaccines against hPIV, RSV and hMPV, we searched literature databases and evaluated both historical and contemporary published research. Results SeV and SeV recombinant vaccines have been tested pre-clinically in a variety of animal models and in Phase I clinical studies. In pre-clinical models, a single dose of SeV induced rapid and long-lasting B- and T-cell responses in the upper respiratory tract and blood. When recombinant SeV constructs were produced and formulated into cocktail vaccines, they were protective against four different respiratory pathogens simultaneously. Vaccines were successful when partnered with passively transferred antibodies; specifically, when a recombinant SeV-based RSV vaccine was tested in the presence of passively transferred monoclonal or polyclonal PIV-specific or RSV-specific antibodies in a cotton rat model, the vaccine provided durable protective immunity against RSV. In clinical trials, SeV was well-tolerated and uniformly immunogenic in PIV-seropositive 1–2 year old children. Methods have been developed for the manufacture of stable SeV-based vaccine products, compatible with wide global distribution of SeV vaccines for clinical use. Conclusion To date, results highlight SeV as an attractive pediatric vaccine candidate. Continued clinical testing of SeV may provide global relief from serious respiratory viral infections in infants and young children.

papers.abstract_zh: 背景 人副流感病毒(hPIV)、呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)和人偏肺病毒(hMPV)等呼吸道病毒对人类构成严重且可能致命的威胁,尤其是对婴儿和幼儿。尽管母源性抗病毒药物和单克隆抗体正在推进以提供对这些病毒的暂时保护,但目前尚未有获批用于儿科的抗病毒药物。副流感病毒(SeV)现在正被开发为一种鼻内给药(I.N.)的候选疫苗,用于预防儿童严重的呼吸道病毒感染。方法 为了评估复制型副流感病毒及其重组体作为针对hPIV、RSV和hMPV的儿科呼吸道病毒疫苗的潜力,我们搜索了文献数据库并评估了历史和现代发表的研究。结果 SeV及其重组体疫苗已在多种动物模型和一期临床研究中进行了临床前测试。在临床前模型中,单次剂量的SeV在上呼吸道和血液中诱导了快速且持久的B细胞和T细胞免疫应答。当重组SeV构建体被制备并配制成混合疫苗时,它们能够同时对四种不同的呼吸道病原体提供保护。当重组SeV为基础的RSV疫苗与被动转移的抗体联合使用时,其在棉花鼠模型中显示出持久的保护性免疫。在临床试验中,SeV在PIV抗体阳性的1-2岁儿童中耐受性良好且具有统一的免疫原性。已经开发出制造稳定SeV为基础的疫苗产品的工艺,使其适用于全球范围内的临床使用。结论 目前的结果突显了SeV作为儿科疫苗候选者的吸引力。持续的临床试验可能为婴儿和幼儿严重的呼吸道病毒感染提供全球性的缓解。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探讨副流感病毒(SeV)作为预防儿童严重呼吸道病毒感染的疫苗候选者的潜力,以应对目前缺乏针对人副流感病毒(hPIV)、呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)和人偏肺病毒(hMPV)的获批儿科疫苗的问题。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究涉及对文献数据库的回顾,以评估SeV及其重组体作为针对hPIV、RSV和hMPV的疫苗的历史和现代研究,但未提供具体的研究设计或人群细节。
analysis_zh.methods: 方法包括搜索文献数据库并评估SeV及其重组体的临床前和临床研究,但未报告详细程序或结果。
analysis_zh.main_results: 结果显示,SeV及其重组体疫苗在动物模型中诱导了快速且持久的免疫应答,并在儿童中表现出良好的耐受性和免疫原性。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为突显SeV作为疫苗候选者的吸引力,并可能为婴儿和幼儿严重的呼吸道病毒感染提供全球性的缓解。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现表明,基于SeV的疫苗可能对多种呼吸道病原体提供保护,从而潜在地减少儿童呼吸道病毒感染的负担。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性包括缺乏随机对照试验,以及需要进一步的临床试验以在更广泛的人群中建立疫苗的有效性和安全性。

papers.title: Temporal dynamics of respiratory pathogens among adult SARI patients in Shanghai, 2019–2023: a multi-center longitudinal surveillance study
papers.abstract: COVID-19 greatly reshaped the epidemiology of severe acute respiratory infection (SARI), yet long-term shifts in multi-pathogen circulation remain poorly characterized.This study explored temporal patterns of common respiratory pathogens among adult SARI patients before, during, and after the pandemic. A retrospective multi-center observational study was performed across seven sentinel hospitals in Shanghai, China (2019–2023). Hospitalized SARI patients aged ≥ 15 years were tested for 12 respiratory pathogens (22 subtypes) using real-time polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR). We stratified the study period into pre-pandemic (2019), pandemic (2020–2022), and post-pandemic (2023) phases for comparative analysis. In total, 4738 participants were enrolled. The overall pathogen detection rate decreased from 30.26% in the pre-pandemic period (2019) to 16.50% during the pandemic (2020–2022), then rebounded to 20.07% in the post-pandemic period (2023) ( P <0.001). A novel classification of four distinct temporal trends was established: (1) decline-resurgence for influenza virus (IFV), Mycoplasma pneumoniae ( M. pneumoniae ), Bordetella pertussis ( B. pertussis ), and human bocavirus (HBoV); (2) sustained decline for human parainfluenza virus (HPIV), human coronavirus (HCoV), human adenovirus (HAdV), human rhinovirus/enterovirus (HRV/EV), and Legionella pneumophila ( L. pneumophila ); (3) transient peak for human metapneumovirus (HMPV); (4) continuous increase for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). IFV, HRV/EV, and HCoV consistently ranked top five across all periods. pneumoniae was the dominant pathogen (33.65%) in patients aged 15–44 years. Seasonal peaks of IFV and RSV were substantially reshaped in the post-pandemic period. The co-infection rate was 1.14% (54/4738), with IFV- M. pneumoniae was the most combination (20.37%). Respiratory pathogen circulation patterns changed substantially from 2019 to 2023. Persistent multi-pathogen surveillance is required to guard against single-pathogen outbreaks and concurrent multi-pathogen epidemics.

papers.title: Beyond Croup: A Phenotype-Based Perspective on Parainfluenza Virus Types in Children
papers.abstract: Human parainfluenza viruses (PIVs) caused an estimated 18.8 million acute lower respiratory infection episodes, 725 000 hospitalizations, and 34 400 deaths among children under 5 in 2018, ranking second only to respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). Despite this burden, clinical attention has historically focused on croup, leading to the common perception that parainfluenza is a single disease entity. However, the 4 types differ substantially in taxonomy, tropism, clinical syndrome, and severity. PIV-1, the most common cause of croup, drives biennial epidemics in toddlers, whereas PIV-2 is less frequent but can cause severe disease, particularly in children with underlying conditions. PIV-3 predominates in young infants, causing bronchiolitis and pneumonia clinically like RSV infection, reflecting its early postnatal susceptibility, which may relate to earlier and more frequent viral exposure. PIV-4, historically underrecognized due to culture limitations, usually does not cause croup but is linked to lower respiratory tract disease, hypoxemia, and occasional neurologic complications. PIV infections are most severe in infants, immunocompromised children, and those in low-resource settings. Seasonal patterns vary by type and geography. Advances in multiplex molecular diagnostics now allow rapid type-specific detection, improving clinical interpretation and management. No vaccine or antiviral is licensed. Emerging therapeutics include sialidase-based antivirals with Food and Drug Administration Breakthrough designation; monoclonal antibodies capable of cross-neutralizing PIV-1, PIV-3, RSV, and human metapneumovirus; and messenger RNA vaccines showing early immunogenicity in children. Recognizing the distinct epidemiology, clinical features, and immune responses of each type is critical for informed pediatric care and the development of targeted preventive and therapeutic strategies.

Despite this burden, clinical attention has historically focused on croup, leading to the common perception that parainfluenza is a single disease entity. However, the 4 types differ substantially in taxonomy, tropism, clinical syndrome, and severity. PIV-1, the most common cause of croup, drives biennial epidemics in toddlers, whereas PIV-2 is less frequent but can cause severe disease, particularly in children with underlying conditions. PIV-3 predominates in young infants, causing bronchiolitis and pneumonia clinically like RSV infection, reflecting its early postnatal susceptibility, which may relate to earlier and more frequent viral exposure. PIV-4, historically underrecognized due to culture limitations, usually does not cause croup but is linked to lower respiratory tract disease, hypoxemia, and occasional neurologic complications. PIV infections are most severe in infants, immunocompromised children, and those in low-resource settings. Seasonal patterns vary by type and geography. Advances in multiplex molecular diagnostics now allow rapid type-specific detection, improving clinical interpretation and management. No vaccine or antiviral is licensed. Emerging therapeutics include sialidase-based antivirals with Food and Drug Administration Breakthrough designation; monoclonal antibodies capable of cross-neutralizing PIV-1, PIV-3, RSV, and human metapneumovirus; and messenger RNA vaccines showing early immunogenicity in children. Recognizing the distinct epidemiology, clinical features, and immune responses of each type is critical for informed pediatric care and the development of targeted preventive and therapeutic strategies.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on human metapneumovirus (hMPV) infection and disease in children. It examines the distinct epidemiology, clinical features, and immune responses of hMPV, emphasizing the need for targeted strategies in pediatric care.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis of existing literature, with no explicit mention of systematic review methods or meta-analysis. It provides general background on hMPV and its clinical relevance without detailing specific databases or eligibility criteria.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that hMPV infections are distinct from other parainfluenza viruses (PIVs) in terms of epidemiology, clinical syndrome, and immune response. It highlights the importance of recognizing these differences for improved clinical management and the development of targeted interventions.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that hMPV has historically been underrecognized due to limitations in diagnostic methods. It also identifies gaps in understanding the full spectrum of hMPV-related diseases and the need for more robust data on its impact in different populations.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that advances in molecular diagnostics are critical for accurate identification of hMPV infections. It also emphasizes the need for further research into hMPV-specific therapeutics and vaccines, as well as improved surveillance and clinical management strategies.

analysis.summary_en: This review highlights the distinct epidemiology, clinical features, and immune responses of human metapneumovirus (hMPV) in children, emphasizing the need for targeted strategies in pediatric care. It notes that hMPV has historically been underrecognized due to diagnostic limitations and underscores the importance of improved surveillance and research into hMPV-specific interventions. The review also identifies gaps in understanding the full spectrum of hMPV-related diseases and calls for further investigation into its impact in different populations.

elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 本综述是对现有文献的叙述性综合,没有明确提到系统综述方法或荟萃分析。它提供了关于hMPV及其临床相关性的总体背景,但未详细说明特定的数据库或纳入排除标准。

elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 综述指出,hMPV由于诊断方法的局限性,历史上被低估。它还指出了对hMPV相关疾病全谱的理解存在不足,以及需要更多关于其在不同人群中影响的可靠数据。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 综述建议,分子诊断技术的进步对于准确识别hMPV感染至关重要。它还强调了需要进一步研究hMPV特异性治疗手段和疫苗,以及改善监测和临床管理策略。

papers.title: Incidence, shedding, and transmission of common respiratory viruses: data from a prospective, longitudinal, household cohort study in the Gambia from March 2021-June 2022.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Respiratory viruses are a major cause of morbidity in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), yet little is known about their incidence, risk factors, and transmission dynamics in community settings. We aimed to compare the epidemiology of multiple respiratory viruses within households in the Gambia. METHODS: We conducted a prospective household cohort study in a peri-urban region of the Gambia. Households with ≥5 members, including at least one adult and one child, were enrolled and followed for one year. Upper respiratory tract swabs were collected weekly, regardless of symptoms, and tested by RT-PCR for SARS-CoV-2, seasonal coronaviruses, human rhinovirus (HRV), influenza A/B, RSV A/B, parainfluenza viruses 1-4, human metapneumovirus, and adenovirus. We estimated incidence, symptomatic fraction, shedding duration, and household secondary attack rates (SARs), and explored associations with virus type and demographic variables. FINDINGS: From 2 March 2021 to 13 June 2022, 349 participants from 52 households completed 14,421 scheduled and 129 unscheduled visits. Respiratory viruses were detected in 11.1% of visits (n = 1611), representing 1423 infection episodes. HRV was most common, infecting 86.5% of participants (2.4 infections per person-year). Children aged <5 and 5-17 years shed virus for longer than adults (p = 0.0005), with longer shedding durations seen for HRV and SARS-CoV-2. Overall, 88.4% of infections were asymptomatic, with the highest symptomatic proportions for SARS-CoV-2 (16.3%) and RSV (17.7%) (p = 0.03). We found evidence for reductions in incidence risk with increasing age for HRV, RSV, seasonal coronaviruses, and parainfluenza viruses, with no difference for SARS-CoV-2. Among 719 index infections, the mean household SARs for all viruses combined was 6.7%. Infection with prolonged shedding (p = 0.002), specific viral species (p < 0.0001) and a lower Ct value were associated with increased transmission. INTERPRETATION: A large burden of asymptomatic infections underlies the circulation of respiratory viruses within households, with key differences in incidence, shedding and transmission across viral species. FUNDING: This study was funded through a UK Research and Innovation grant.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 呼吸道病毒是低收入和中等收入国家(LMICs)发病率的主要原因之一,但在社区环境中对其传播、风险因素和感染动态了解甚少。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们在冈比亚的一个郊区地区开展了一项前瞻性家庭研究。纳入了至少有5名成员、包括至少一名成人和一名儿童的家庭,并进行了为期一年的随访。

elements_zh.main_results: From 2 March 2021 to 13 June 2022, 349 participants from 52 households completed 14,421 scheduled and 129 unscheduled visits. Respiratory viruses were detected in 11.1% of visits (n = 1611), representing 1423 infection episodes. HRV was most common, infecting 86.5% of participants (2.4 infections per person-year). Children aged <5 and 5-17 years shed virus for longer than adults (p = 0.0005), with longer shedding durations seen for HRV and SARS-CoV-2. Overall, 88.4% of infections were asymptomatic, with the highest symptomatic proportions for SARS-CoV-2 (16.3%) and RSV (17.7%) (p = 0.03).
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 在家庭中,呼吸道病毒的传播主要由大量无症状感染驱动,不同病毒种类在传播、排毒和持续性方面存在关键差异。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为社区环境中呼吸道病毒的防控策略和风险评估提供依据,特别是强调无症状感染在家庭传播中的作用。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究仅在冈比亚的一个郊区地区进行,限制了其普遍适用性。由于样本量大且数据收集全面,证据强度较强。

news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Thursday, November 19, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health RSV Activity and Interference Shape Human Metapneumovirus Timing in US Study by November 17, 2026 in Biology, Health Reading Time: 2 mins read 0 RSV Activity and Interference Shape Human Metapneumovirus Timing in US Study Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram Transmission rates of human metapneumovirus (HMPV) are shaped by viral interference from respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) rather than regional climate conditions, according to an age-stratified dynamic transmission modeling study conducted by Ke Li and colleagues. HMPV causes acute lower respiratory infections that primarily affect young children and older adults, generating seasonal outbreaks that peak annually in March or April across the United States and other temperate regions in the Northern hemisphere. To determine the poorly understood drivers of this seasonality, the research team analyzed laboratory-confirmed HMPV cases alongside age-specific emergency department visits across ten distinct US regions. The researchers tested several candidate transmission models to evaluate whether environmental factors or viral interference governed observed spatiotemporal patterns. Dynamic models incorporating climate variables into the transmission rate, including vapor pressure, precipitation, potential evapotranspiration, and minimum temperature, could not capture the timing of HMPV activity across all ten regions. In contrast, the timing of HMPV outbreaks was consistently associated with RSV activity, demonstrating that the HMPV transmission rate is directly reduced in the presence of circulating RSV. This viral interference proved essential for explaining regional variations in infection cycles. Among the candidate models analyzed, only those incorporating an RSV-associated term successfully reproduced the biennial patterns of HMPV documented in certain regions. These multi-year cycles are characterized by alternating epidemic waves classified by the authors as “late-small” and “early-large” outbreaks, a dynamic that purely climate-driven formulations failed to replicate. Discover more Find Lung Care Check Symptoms Read Med Journals respiratory syncytial virus Respiratory syncytial virus Using the best-fit model containing the RSV-associated term, the investigators predicted how future RSV interventions might influence HMPV spread. Although RSV interventions reduce viral competition between the two pathogens, model forecasts indicate that such measures are unlikely to result in a substantial increase in HMPV activity. The authors concluded that defining these spatiotemporal dynamics and pathogen interactions will help inform future seasonal forecasting and intervention strategies for HMPV. news.source_body_en: A study published on November 17, 2026, by Bioengineer.org, led by Ke Li and colleagues, found that the timing of human metapneumovirus (HMPV) outbreaks in the United States is shaped by viral interference from respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), rather than regional climate conditions. The research team analyzed laboratory-confirmed HMPV cases and age-specific emergency department visits across ten US regions, using age-stratified dynamic transmission modeling. They tested several candidate models, including those incorporating climate variables like vapor pressure, precipitation, and temperature, but found these could not capture the timing of HMPV activity. The study concluded that understanding these dynamics will aid in forecasting and intervention strategies for HMPV. The findings are confirmed based on the analysis of HMPV outbreaks and their association with RSV activity.

supplementary_news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Thursday, November 19, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health RSV Activity and Interference Shape Human Metapneumovirus Timing in US Study by November 17, 2026 in Biology, Health Reading Time: 2 mins read 0 RSV Activity and Interference Shape Human Metapneumovirus Timing in US Study Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram Transmission rates of human metapneumovirus (HMPV) are shaped by viral interference from respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) rather than regional climate conditions, according to an age-stratified dynamic transmission modeling study conducted by Ke Li and colleagues. HMPV causes acute lower respiratory infections that primarily affect young children and older adults, generating seasonal outbreaks that peak annually in March or April across the United States and other temperate regions in the Northern hemisphere. To determine the poorly understood drivers of this seasonality, the research team analyzed laboratory-confirmed HMPV cases alongside age-specific emergency department visits across ten distinct US regions. The researchers tested several candidate transmission models to evaluate whether environmental factors or viral interference governed observed spatiotemporal patterns. Dynamic models incorporating climate variables into the transmission rate, including vapor pressure, precipitation, potential evapotranspiration, and minimum temperature, could not capture the timing of HMPV activity across all ten regions. In contrast, the timing of HMPV outbreaks was consistently associated with RSV activity, demonstrating that the HMPV transmission rate is directly reduced in the presence of circulating RSV. This viral interference proved essential for explaining regional variations in infection cycles. Among the candidate models analyzed, only those incorporating an RSV-associated term successfully reproduced the biennial patterns of HMPV documented in certain regions. These multi-year cycles are characterized by alternating epidemic waves classified by the authors as “late-small” and “early-large” outbreaks, a dynamic that purely climate-driven formulations failed to replicate. Using the best-fit model containing the RSV-associated term, the investigators predicted how future RSV interventions might influence HMPV spread. Although RSV interventions reduce viral competition between the two pathogens, model forecasts indicate that such measures are unlikely to result in a substantial increase in HMPV activity. The authors concluded that defining these spatiotemporal dynamics and pathogen interactions will help inform future seasonal forecasting and intervention strategies for HMPV. Subject of Research: Spatiotemporal dynamics and RSV viral interference of human metapneumovirus Article Title: Spatiotemporal dynamics of human metapneumovirus and potential impact of respiratory syncytial virus interventions in the United States Article References: Li, K., Perniciaro, S., Kwon, J., Grubaugh, N. D., Weinberger, D. M., & Pitzer, V. E. (2026). Spatiotemporal dynamics of human metapneumovirus and potential impact of respiratory syncytial virus interventions in the United States.
